title: A CaLLM Judge is a Better Judge: Mitigating Bias in LLM-as-a-judge
abstract: arXiv:2610.18108v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used as judges to predict which of two candidate answers a human evaluator would prefer, providing a scalable alternative when human evaluation is too costly. Unfortunately, LLM judgments can exhibit systematic biases. Prior work has documented position, verbosity or model family of the candidate answers influencing the judge decision rather than their quality, while additional biases may remain undocumented. $\textit{Multicalibration}$ provides a natural framework to address this problem: each bias corresponds to miscalibration on an identifiable group, $\textit{e.g.}$, family bias manifests as overconfidence in answers generated by models belonging to the same family of the judge. The challenge is to fix miscalibration simultaneously across many, potentially unknown groups. translated_title: CaLLM裁判是更好的裁判：缓解LLM-as-a-judge中的偏差
translated_abstract: 大语言模型（LLM）越来越多地被用作裁判，以预测人类评估者会更偏好两个候选答案中的哪一个，从而在人工评估成本过高时提供一种可扩展的替代方案。遗憾的是，LLM的判断可能表现出系统性的偏差。先前的研究已经记录了候选答案的位置、冗长度或所属模型族会影响裁判的决策，而非答案本身的质量，此外还可能存在未被记录的其他偏差。多重校准为解决这一问题提供了一个自然的框架：每种偏差都对应于某个可识别群体上的校准失准，例如，模型族偏差表现为裁判对由与其同族的模型生成的答案过度自信。挑战在于如何同时在许多（可能是未知的）群体上修复校准失准。为此，我们提出了CaLLM，这是一个事后（post hoc）框架，可以对LLM裁判进行多重校准，从而约束……（摘要原文在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文提出CaLLM——一种事后多重校准框架，能够同时在许多可能未知的群体上修复LLM裁判的校准失准，从而缓解LLM-as-a-judge中的系统性偏差。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces CaLLM, a post hoc multicalibration framework that simultaneously corrects miscalibration across many potentially unknown groups, thereby mitigating systematic biases in LLM-as-a-judge.
